data.title: FAA poised to approve Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week - Reuters
data.description:
The Federal Aviation Administration ‌is set to approve the long-delayed Boeing (BA) 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week after completing a key safety review, Reuters reported Friday.

In one of the last steps prior to final approval, the FAA and Boeing (BA) reportedly held a successful meeting Friday of the Type Certification Board, which is comprised of agency management team members.

Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for ~30% of Boeing's (BA) outstanding ​737 backlog, but numerous delays have helped European rival Airbus' A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market.

A glitch with the latest update ​of the 737 ⁠MAX's navigation software threatened to further delay certification when Boeing (BA) disclosed it last month, but the FAA determined it did not pose a safety concern and did not require a fix as ​a condition of certifying the plane.

Boeing (BA) is still working on certifying ​the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production and six years behind schedule.

data.title: Coca-Cola advances for its seventh consecutive session
data.description:
Coca-Cola (KO) extended its rally for the seventh consecutive trading session, with shares closing 2.07% higher at $93.90.

KO has gained 7.20% over the past six trading sessions, while the benchmark S&P 500 Index declined 0.74%. Year to date, the stock has returned 33.40%, compared with a 13.13% gain in the S&P 500.

Adding to the company's growth prospects, Coca-Cola will become the beverage supplier for KFC locations across the U.S., with the rollout expected to reach all locations by spring 2027. TD Cowen estimates the partnership could contribute 10–20 basis points to KO's total revenue in 2027. The brokerage also highlighted KO's market-share gains in carbonated soft drinks over the past two years, while PepsiCo lost share.

Despite the strong share-price performance, Seeking Alpha analyst Endurance Investing maintained a Hold rating on KO, citing its high valuation and an ongoing IRS tax dispute that could result in an additional $14 billion liability, which the analyst believes is not fully priced into the stock.

Meanwhile, Seeking Alpha analyst Muhammad Din Cheema rated KO a Buy, citing its strong brand, high-margin business model, growth opportunities in emerging markets, and consistent dividend track record.

Seeking Alpha's Quant rating assigned KO a Hold with a score of 3.46 out of 5, with an A+ grade for profitability, a B for growth, and an F for valuation.

Wall Street analysts were more bullish, with 19 rating the stock Buy or higher, four assigning a Hold, and one rating it Sell or lower.

Separately, Seeking Alpha analysts were more cautious, giving KO a Hold rating with an average score of 2.83 out of 5.

data.title: Tech stocks drag Nasdaq 2% lower; sheds over 4% for the week
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) plunged 2.14% on Friday as technology stocks came under pressure.

Traders wrapped a mostly losing week amid a pullback in artificial intelligence-related stocks, with memory chip stocks among the hardest-hit segments as investors reassessed the sector's recent performance.

Semiconductor stocks suffered, with Micron Technology (MU) ending 5.63% lower in the session. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) lost 5.97%, while Sandisk (SNDK) declined 6.85%.

The tech-heavy index was on track for its worst week since June, as per CNBC. For the week, Nasdaq lost 4.48%.

The weekly decliners, however, were led by Rocket Lab (RKLB), which lost more than 25% over the week after the space launch company pushed the inaugural flight of its Neutron rocket into 2027.

Meanwhile, consumer stocks made up most of the week’s gainers amid a broader tech sell-off. Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) notched the highest gains after Piper Sandler upgraded the beverage stock to an Overweight earlier in the week.

data.title: Compass sues California's listing service over anti-competitive rules - report
data.description:
Compass (COMP) has sued the California Regional Multiple Listing Service for allegedly adopting anti-competitive rules, Bloomberg News reported on Friday.

The federal court suit filed in Los Angeles reportedly alleges that CRMLS's requirement that agents list homes for sale within one business day or face fines violates U.S. antitrust laws, according to the report.

CRMLS is "dictating how Compass and its agents can and cannot compete, how Compass and its agents can and cannot serve their clients, and how homeowners can and cannot market their own homes," the company reportedly said.

The listing service had sued Compass earlier this month in New York, seeking a court order in support of its listings rules. According to the listing service, Compass wants to publicly advertise homes on its platform while withholding those same listings from the shared database, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: The stock market is pricing in ‘too many rate hikes’ – Allianz’s El-Erian
data.description:
Markets are pricing in too many interest rate hikes, according to Mohamed, chief economic adviser at Allianz.

In an interview with CNBC, El-Erian said expectations of three total hikes by September are excessive despite recent dovish interpretations of Federal Reserve messaging.

El-Erian noted that while markets currently see less than a 20% probability of an October rate hike and nearly 90% odds of a December increase, the outlook beyond that is overblown.

"The market is pricing in a total of two and a half hikes by the middle of next year, three by September. I think that's too much," he said.

He added that the market has "a behavioral bias to reading something that is dovish when it's not hawkish," which explains the current rate expectations.

The economist expressed concern about interest-rate-sensitive segments of the economy and warned that weakness in the technology sector (XLK) could create broader problems.

"If the selloff in tech continues, that could [be] an economic and technical dampener on other things," El-Erian said.

He cautioned against the popular rotation trade away from tech stocks, noting that tech has been "a major magnet for lots of international and domestic flows into the market."

El-Erian acknowledged that the Federal Reserve cannot ignore recent inflation data, which has come in above expectations. This inflationary pressure keeps the possibility of further rate action on the table beyond December.

While the market expects continued rate increases after December, El-Erian remains skeptical.

"The question is, do they keep going after December? The market thinks they will. I'm not so sure," he said.

He pointed to underlying concerns about the economy, particularly segments sensitive to higher interest rates, as reasons the Fed may pause sooner than markets anticipate.
